question:
Select the most appropriate homonym to fill in the blank.
Please ___________more sugar to the juice so that it becomes sweeter.
options: ad
add
aide
aid
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "add"


Explanation:
☛ The sentence talks about 'mixing sugar in the juice,' for which the correct word is 'add' (to put something together).
☛ 'ad' means 'advertisement,' which is irrelevant here.
☛ 'aide' (assistant) and 'aid' (help) do not fit the context of the sentence.
☛ Choosing the right homonym requires understanding the sentence's context and the meaning of words.


Grammar Rules:
☛ Homonyms are words that sound alike but have different meanings and spellings.
☛ The sentence requires a verb, so 'add' (a verb) is the correct choice.
☛ Exams often confuse students with homonyms, so remember the exact meaning and usage of such words.
question_hi:
Select the most appropriate homonym to fill in the blank.
Please ___________more sugar to the juice so that it becomes sweeter.
options_hi: ad
add
aide
aid
solution_hi:
Solution: Correct Answer is "add"


Explanation:
☛ यहाँ वाक्य में 'चीनी को जूस में मिलाने' की बात कही गई है, जिसके लिए सही शब्द 'add' (जोड़ना) है।
☛ 'ad' का अर्थ है 'विज्ञापन', जो इस संदर्भ में अनुपयुक्त है।
☛ 'aide' और 'aid' का अर्थ क्रमशः 'सहायक' और 'सहायता' है, जो वाक्य के अर्थ से मेल नहीं खाते।
☛ Homonyms (समोच्चारित शब्द) में सही विकल्प चुनने के लिए वाक्य के संदर्भ और शब्दों के अर्थ को समझना आवश्यक है।


Grammar Rules:
☛ Homonyms वे शब्द होते हैं जिनकी ध्वनि समान होती है, लेकिन अर्थ और वर्तनी अलग-अलग होती है।
☛ वाक्य में क्रिया (verb) की आवश्यकता है, इसलिए 'add' (क्रिया) सही विकल्प है।
☛ परीक्षा में अक्सर समोच्चारित शब्दों के बीच भ्रम पैदा किया जाता है, इसलिए शब्दों के सही अर्थ और प्रयोग को याद रखें।

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
The ________ of the whale is 2 tonnes.
options: wait
weight
vet
wet
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "weight"


Explanation:
☛ The sentence discusses the 'whale' and mentions its measurement (2 tonnes), which clearly refers to its mass.
☛ Among the options, 'weight' is the only term that logically fits here as it denotes the heaviness of an object.
☛ 'Wait' means to stay in expectation, 'vet' means an animal doctor, and 'wet' means soaked in liquid – all irrelevant in this context.
☛ 'Weight' is a noun representing physical mass, aligning perfectly with the sentence's subject.


Grammar Rules:
☛ Noun Usage: 'Weight' is a noun describing the measure of heaviness. Here, it acts as the subject complement after the linking verb 'is'.
☛ Sentence Structure: The pattern is Subject (The whale) + Verb (is) + Complement (2 tonnes), where 'weight' bridges the subject and its attribute.
☛ Homophones Alert: Exams often test homophones (e.g., wait/weight). Contextual understanding is key to avoiding confusion.
☛ Units of Measurement: Words like 'tonnes' typically pair with measurable nouns (e.g., weight, height), not abstract ones.
question_hi:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

options_hi: wait
weight
vet
wet
solution_hi:
Solution: Correct Answer is "weight"

☛ यहाँ वाक्य में 'whale' (व्हेल) के बारे में बात की जा रही है और उसके वजन (2 टन) का उल्लेख किया गया है।
☛ दिए गए विकल्पों में से 'weight' (वजन) ही सही शब्द है जो इस संदर्भ में फिट बैठता है।
☛ 'Wait' का अर्थ है 'प्रतीक्षा करना', 'vet' का अर्थ है 'पशु चिकित्सक', और 'wet' का अर्थ है 'गीला' – ये सभी विकल्प अर्थहीन हैं।
☛ 'Weight' एक संज्ञा (noun) है जो किसी वस्तु के भार को दर्शाती है, जो वाक्य के विषय से मेल खाती है।


Grammar Rules:
☛ संज्ञा (Noun): 'Weight' एक संज्ञा है जो भौतिक वस्तुओं के भार को दर्शाती है। वाक्य में इसका प्रयोग विषय (whale) की विशेषता बताने के लिए हुआ है।
☛ वाक्य संरचना: Subject (The whale) + Linking Verb (is) + Complement (2 tonnes) के बीच में 'weight' जैसी संज्ञा का प्रयोग होता है।
☛ समानार्थक शब्दों का ध्यान: परीक्षा में अक्सर समान ध्वनि वाले शब्द (जैसे wait/weight) दिए जाते हैं, इसलिए संदर्भ को समझना आवश्यक है।

question:
Fill in the blank using the correct collocation.
We need to ________ a decision on the housing project tomorrow morning.
options: make
draw
build
frame
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "make"

Explanation:
☛ The correct collocation here is "make a decision", which means "to decide something."
☛ Collocations are word pairs or groups that naturally go together in English.
☛ Other options like "draw", "build", or "frame" do not collocate with "decision".
☛ The verb "make" is commonly used with abstract nouns such as "make a plan", "make a choice", and "make a mistake".

Grammar Rules:
☛ Collocations are essential in English to make sentences sound natural and correct.
☛ Some common collocations include:
- Make: make a decision, make a difference, make a noise
- Take: take a break, take a chance, take a photo
- Do: do homework, do business, do a favor
question_hi:

options_hi: make
draw
build
frame

Explanation:
☛ यहाँ पर "make a decision" एक सही और सामान्यत: प्रयोग किया जाने वाला collocation है, जिसका अर्थ है "निर्णय लेना"।
☛ Collocation शब्दों का ऐसा समूह होता है जो एक साथ प्राकृतिक रूप से प्रयोग किए जाते हैं।
☛ अन्य विकल्प जैसे "draw", "build", या "frame" का प्रयोग "decision" के साथ नहीं किया जाता है।
☛ "Make" का प्रयोग अक्सर abstract चीजों जैसे "make a plan", "make a choice", "make a mistake" आदि के साथ किया जाता है।

Grammar Rules:
☛ Collocations अंग्रेजी भाषा का एक महत्वपूर्ण हिस्सा हैं जो वाक्य को प्राकृतिक और सही बनाते हैं।
☛ कुछ common collocations हैं:
- Make: make a decision, make a difference, make a noise
- Take: take a break, take a chance, take a photo
- Do: do homework, do business, do a favor

question:
Select the correct collocation to complete the following sentence.

He made __________ use of the opportunity to travel.
options: full
total
entire
whole
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "full"

Explanation:
☛ Here, 'full use' is the correct collocation, meaning 'complete utilization'.
☛ 'Full' pairs naturally with 'use' in this context, giving the sentence its intended meaning.
☛ While 'total', 'entire', and 'whole' are synonyms, they do not collocate with 'use' in the same way.
☛ Collocations are crucial in English as they represent natural word pairings.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Collocations are groups of two or more words that frequently go together.
☛ 'Make full use of' is a common collocation meaning 'to take complete advantage of something'.
☛ Other examples: 'heavy rain', 'strong coffee', 'fast food'.
☛ Learning collocations improves fluency and makes speech sound more natural.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Collocations दो या अधिक शब्दों का ऐसा समूह होता है जो अक्सर साथ प्रयोग किया जाता है।
☛ 'Make full use of' एक सामान्य collocation है जिसका अर्थ है 'किसी चीज़ का पूरा फायदा उठाना'।
☛ अन्य उदाहरण: 'heavy rain', 'strong coffee', 'fast food'।
☛ Collocations को याद रखना और समझना fluency बढ़ाने में मदद करता है।

question:
Choose an appropriate word that can substitute the bracketed word and complete the sentence meaningfully.
What is the time (in) your watch?
options: by
with
into
on
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "by"

Explanation:
☛ The sentence asks for the time according to the watch.
☛ 'By' is the correct preposition here because it indicates the source (the watch) that provides the time.
☛ 'In' suggests being inside something, which is irrelevant here.
☛ 'With' means 'accompanied by,' which doesn't fit the context.
☛ 'Into' (movement inward) and 'on' (surface contact) are grammatically incorrect here.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Preposition 'by' is used to denote agency, means, or reference.
☛ Example: "The letter was sent by post." (Means)
☛ It also indicates proximity in time/place, e.g., "She sat by the window."
☛ Avoid confusing it with 'with' (tool) or 'in' (enclosure).
question_hi:
Choose an appropriate word that can substitute the bracketed word and complete the sentence meaningfully.
What is the time (in) your watch?
options_hi: by
with
into
on
solution_hi:
Solution: Correct Answer is "by"

Explanation:
☛ यहाँ वाक्य में 'watch' (घड़ी) के साथ समय पूछा जा रहा है।
☛ 'By' preposition का प्रयोग यहाँ इसलिए सही है क्योंकि यह किसी विशेष स्रोत (यहाँ घड़ी) के अनुसार समय बताने के लिए प्रयुक्त होता है।
☛ 'In' का प्रयोग स्थान या समय के अंदर होने का भाव देता है, जो यहाँ उचित नहीं है।
☛ 'With' का अर्थ है 'साथ में', जो यहाँ अर्थपूर्ण नहीं है।
☛ 'Into' और 'on' भी इस संदर्भ में अनुपयुक्त हैं।

Grammar Rules:
☛ Preposition 'by' का प्रयोग किसी माध्यम, स्रोत या तरीके को दर्शाने के लिए किया जाता है।
☛ उदाहरण: "The book was written by him." (माध्यम)
☛ 'By' का प्रयोग समय या स्थान के नजदीकी को भी दर्शाता है, जैसे: "He was standing by the door.

question:
Complete the following sentence.

He ______ to the manager about the terrible food in the hostel.
options: He made a complaint .
He terribly complained.
He said a complaint .
He said a big complaint .
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "He made a complaint ."


Explanation:

☛The correct answer is "made a complaint" because "complaint" is a noun and it collocates with the verb "make".
☛The phrase "make a complaint" is a fixed expression meaning 'to formally express dissatisfaction'.
☛Other options like "terribly complained" or "said a complaint" are grammatically incorrect. "Complained" is a verb and doesn't pair well with "terribly" in this context, while "say" isn't used with "complaint".
☛The sentence structure Subject (He) + Verb (made) + Object (a complaint) + Prepositional Phrase (to the manager...) is perfectly correct.



Grammar Rules:

☛Make vs Do: Use "make" for creating/producing something (e.g., "make a plan"), and "do" for general actions (e.g., "do homework").
☛Collocations: Certain verb-noun pairs are fixed in English. Examples: "make a decision", "take a shower". "Make a complaint" follows this rule.
☛Adverb Placement: Adverbs usually follow verbs, but "terribly complained" sounds unnatural. Better: "complained bitterly".
☛Reporting Verbs: With nouns like "complaint", use "make", not "say". Compare: "He said (that) the food was bad" (correct) vs "He said a complaint" (incorrect).
question_hi:
Complete the following sentence.

He ______ to the manager about the terrible food in the hostel.
options_hi: He made a complaint .
He terribly complained.
He said a complaint .
He said a big complaint .
solution_hi:
Solution: Correct Answer is "He made a complaint ."


Explanation:

☛यहाँ "made a complaint" सही विकल्प है क्योंकि "complaint" (शिकायत) एक संज्ञा (noun) है और इसके साथ "make" क्रिया (verb) का प्रयोग होता है।
☛"Make a complaint" एक स्थिर वाक्यांश (fixed phrase) है जिसका अर्थ है 'शिकायत करना'।
☛अन्य विकल्प जैसे "terribly complained" या "said a complaint" व्याकरणिक रूप से गलत हैं क्योंकि "complain" क्रिया के साथ "terribly" (क्रिया विशेषण) का प्रयोग असंगत है और "say" क्रिया का प्रयोग "complaint" के साथ नहीं होता।
☛वाक्य संरचना (sentence structure) के अनुसार Subject (He) + Verb (made) + Object (a complaint) + Prepositional Phrase (to the manager...) पूर्णतः सही है।



Grammar Rules:

☛Make vs Do: "Make" का प्रयोग निर्माण या सृजन (creation) के अर्थ में होता है जबकि "Do" का प्रयोग कार्य (action) के लिए होता है। उदाहरण: "make a plan" (योजना बनाना), "do homework" (गृहकार्य करना)।
☛Collocations: अंग्रेजी में कुछ क्रिया-संज्ञा जोड़े (verb-noun pairs) स्थिर होते हैं। जैसे: "make a decision" (निर्णय लेना), "take a shower" (नहाना)। "Make a complaint" भी ऐसा ही एक उदाहरण है।
☛Adverb Placement: क्रिया विशेषण (adverb) आमतौर पर क्रिया के बाद आते हैं, लेकिन "terribly complained" में यह अर्थ को अस्पष्ट कर देता है। सही प्रयोग होगा: "complained bitterly"।

question:
Select the most appropriate article to fill in the blank (ø-no article).
_________ SDO is the head of the sub-division of ___ government organisation.
options: an; a
a; a
Ø; a
an; ø
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "an; a"

Explanation:
☛ The first blank uses "an" because "SDO" is pronounced as "es-dee-oh," starting with a vowel sound 'e.' English grammar rules state that "an" is used before words with a vowel sound.
☛ The second blank uses "a" because "government" starts with a consonant sound 'g.' Words beginning with consonant sounds take "a" as the article.
☛ Here, "government organisation" is a common noun, requiring an indefinite article (a/an) for generalization.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Indefinite Articles (a/an): These are used with non-specific nouns.
- "a" is used before words starting with a consonant sound.
- "an" is used before words starting with a vowel sound (a, e, i, o, u).
☛ Pronunciation Matters: Some words start with a vowel in spelling but have a consonant sound (e.g., university, European). Such words take "a" instead of "an.
question_hi:
Select the most appropriate article to fill in the blank (ø-no article).
_________ SDO is the head of the sub-division of ___ government organisation.
options_hi: an; a
a; a
Ø; a
an; ø
solution_hi:
Solution: Correct Answer is "an; a"

Explanation:
☛ पहले खाली स्थान में "an" का प्रयोग किया गया है क्योंकि "SDO" का उच्चारण "एस-डी-ओ" होता है, जो एक स्वर (vowel sound) 'ए' से शुरू होता है। अंग्रेजी व्याकरण के नियमानुसार, स्वर ध्वनि से शुरू होने वाले शब्दों से पहले "an" का प्रयोग किया जाता है।
☛ दूसरे खाली स्थान में "a" का प्रयोग किया गया है क्योंकि "government" शब्द एक व्यंजन ध्वनि 'ग' से शुरू होता है। व्यंजन ध्वनि से शुरू होने वाले शब्दों से पहले "a" का प्रयोग होता है।
☛ यहाँ "government organisation" एक सामान्य संज्ञा (common noun) है, जिसके लिए indefinite article (a/an) का प्रयोग आवश्यक है।

Grammar Rules:
☛ Indefinite Articles (a/an): ये अनिश्चित संज्ञाओं (non-specific nouns) के साथ प्रयोग किए जाते हैं।
- "a" का प्रयोग व्यंजन ध्वनि (consonant sound) से शुरू होने वाले शब्दों से पहले किया जाता है।
- "an" का प्रयोग स्वर ध्वनि (vowel sound - a, e, i, o, u) से शुरू होने वाले शब्दों से पहले किया जाता है।
☛ Pronunciation Matters: कुछ शब्द वर्तनी (spelling) में स्वर से शुरू होते हैं, लेकिन उच्चारण व्यंजन से होता है (जैसे - university, European)। ऐसे शब्दों से पहले "a" का प्रयोग होता है।

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
She ________ her painting by this time next week.
options: finishes
will finish
will have finished
finished
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "will have finished"

Explanation:
☛ The sentence refers to a future point in time ("by this time next week") where the action (completing the painting) will already be completed.
☛ The Future Perfect Tense is used for actions that will be finished before a specific future time.
☛ Structure: will + have + V3 (past participle) → "will have finished" is correct as "finished" is the V3 form of "finish".
☛ Other options (finishes – Simple Present, will finish – Simple Future, finished – Simple Past) are incorrect as they don’t convey completion relative to a future timeframe.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Future Perfect Tense describes actions that will be completed before a specified future time.
☛ Often used with time expressions like "by + time", "by then", or "before".
☛ Example: "She will have submitted the report before the deadline."
☛ Common Errors: Using "will finish" (implies simple future, not completion). Always check for time clues (e.g., "by") to identify the correct tense.
question_hi:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
She ________ her painting by this time next week.
options_hi: finishes
will finish
will have finished
finished
solution_hi:
Solution: Correct Answer is "will have finished"

Explanation:
☛ यहाँ वाक्य में भविष्य के एक निश्चित समय ("by this time next week") की बात की गई है जब कार्य (पेंटिंग पूरी करना) पहले ही समाप्त हो चुका होगा।
☛ Future Perfect Tense का प्रयोग ऐसे ही संदर्भों में किया जाता है, जहाँ भविष्य में किसी निर्धारित समय से पहले कार्य पूरा हो जाएगा।
☛ संरचना: will + have + V3 (past participle) → "will have finished" सही है क्योंकि "finish" का V3 रूप "finished" है।
☛ अन्य विकल्प (finishes – Simple Present, will finish – Simple Future, finished – Simple Past) इस संदर्भ में असंगत हैं क्योंकि वे कार्य की पूर्णता को भविष्य के सापेक्ष व्यक्त नहीं करते।

question:

☛ Other options like "under", "over", or "below" are inappropriate in this context as they don't convey the intended meaning.

Grammar Rules:
☛ "Above" is a preposition indicating spatial or qualitative superiority.
☛ Fixed phrases like "above suspicion", "above reproach" always use "above".
☛ Prepositions must be chosen according to context and intended meaning.
☛ "Under suspicion" would mean 'being suspected', which is opposite to the intended meaning here.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.
Each one of the participants in the annual function ________ an applause.
options: is deserving
have deserved
deserve
deserves
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "deserves"


Explanation:

☛The subject of the sentence is "Each one of the participants", which is singular because "Each one" is a singular term.
☛The verb must agree with the singular subject, hence "deserves" is the correct option.
☛Other options like "deserve" (plural), "have deserved" (present perfect, plural), and "is deserving" (continuous form) are incorrect here as they do not agree with the subject.
☛The sentence means: "Each one of the participants in the annual function deserves an applause."



Grammar Rules:

☛Subject-Verb Agreement: Use a singular verb with a singular subject and a plural verb with a plural subject.
☛Words like "Each," "Every," "Either," "Neither" are followed by a singular verb.
☛Present Indefinite Tense: Used to express general truths, habitual actions, or present events.

☛ Other options like "my", "their", and "our" are possessive adjectives, which require a noun (e.g., "my car", "their house", "our school").
☛ Since there is no noun after the blank, "mine" is the correct choice.

- Incorrect: "This pen is my." (my cannot stand alone)

question:

options: is examining
examines
will be examining
had examined
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "had examined"

Explanation:
☛ The sentence describes two actions: (1) Gautam checking the documents and (2) the senior advocate reaching the court.
☛ Since the examination of documents was completed before the senior advocate arrived, the Past Perfect Tense (had + V3) is used.

☛ Other options like "is examining" (Present Continuous), "examines" (Simple Present), and "will be examining" (Future Continuous) are grammatically incorrect here as they do not fit the timeline.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Past Perfect Tense (had + V3) is used for actions completed before another action in the past.
☛ It emphasizes the sequence of two past events.
☛ Words like "by the time", "before", or "after" often signal the need for Past Perfect Tense.
☛ Always check the timeline of actions to decide between Simple Past and Past Perfect.

question:

options: stay

have stayed
stayed
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "will stay"

Explanation:
☛ The sentence follows the First Conditional structure, which uses the pattern: If + Present Simple, will + base verb.
☛ "If I go to Bangalore" is in the Present Simple tense, indicating a possible future action.
☛ The correct response is will stay because it shows a future action resulting from the condition.
☛ Other options like stay (without 'will'), have stayed (Present Perfect), and stayed (Past Simple) are incorrect as they do not fit the conditional structure.

Grammar Rules:
☛ The First Conditional is used for real or possible situations.
☛ The If Clause (condition) is in the Present Simple, and the Main Clause (result) uses will + base verb.
☛ Example: If she studies hard, she will pass the exam.

Explanation:
☛ यहाँ वाक्य में First Conditional (पहली शर्त) का प्रयोग हुआ है, जो If + Present Simple, will + base verb के पैटर्न का अनुसरण करता है।
☛ "If I go to Bangalore" (यदि मैं बैंगलोर जाता हूँ) एक Present Simple वाक्य है, जो भविष्य में होने वाली संभावित घटना को दर्शाता है।
☛ इसके बाद will stay का प्रयोग किया गया है, क्योंकि यह भविष्य में होने वाली क्रिया को दर्शाता है।
☛ अन्य विकल्प जैसे stay (बिना 'will' के), have stayed (Present Perfect), और stayed (Past Simple) इस संदर्भ में गलत हैं क्योंकि वे Conditional Structure का पालन नहीं करते।

Grammar Rules:
☛ First Conditional का प्रयोग वास्तविक या संभावित स्थितियों के लिए किया जाता है।
☛ इसमें If Clause (शर्त वाला भाग) Present Simple में होता है, और Main Clause (मुख्य भाग) will + base verb में होता है।
☛ उदाहरण: If it rains, we will cancel the trip. (यदि बारिश होती है, हम यात्रा रद्द कर देंगे।)

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
The air quality is so bad ______it becomes difficult to breathe.
options: that
since
as
when
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "that"

Explanation:
☛ Here, the sentence uses the "so...that" structure, which acts as a conjunction.
☛ "so...that" is used to show cause and effect, where the first part states the cause and the second part states the result.
☛ In this case, the effect of bad air quality is difficulty in breathing, so "that" is the correct choice.
☛ Other options like "since" (because), "as" (while), and "when" (at the time) are not suitable here because they indicate time or reason, not a result.

Grammar Rules:
☛ "so...that" is a correlative conjunction that connects two clauses.
☛ "so" is followed by an adjective/adverb, and "that" introduces the result clause.
☛ It is used to show the degree of effect.
☛ Example: "She was so happy that she cried."
question_hi:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
The air quality is so bad ______it becomes difficult to breathe.
options_hi: that
since
as
when
solution_hi:
Solution: Correct Answer is "that"

Explanation:
☛ यहाँ वाक्य में "so...that" का प्रयोग किया गया है, जो एक conjunction के रूप में कार्य करता है।
☛ "so...that" का प्रयोग cause and effect (कारण और प्रभाव) दिखाने के लिए किया जाता है, जहाँ पहला भाग कारण बताता है और दूसरा भाग उसका परिणाम।
☛ यहाँ वायु गुणवत्ता खराब होने का परिणाम साँस लेने में कठिनाई है, इसलिए "that" सही विकल्प है।
☛ अन्य विकल्प जैसे "since" (क्योंकि), "as" (जैसा कि), और "when" (जब) इस संदर्भ में उपयुक्त नहीं हैं क्योंकि वे परिणाम दिखाने के लिए नहीं बल्कि समय या कारण बताने के लिए प्रयुक्त होते हैं।

Grammar Rules:
☛ "so...that" एक correlative conjunction है जो दो clauses को जोड़ता है।
☛ "so" के बाद adjective/adverb आता है और "that" के बाद result clause।
☛ इसका प्रयोग degree of effect (प्रभाव की मात्रा) दिखाने के लिए किया जाता है।
☛ उदाहरण: "He was so tired that he fell asleep immediately."

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.
Hurry up ! There’s still ________ work left to do.
options: whole
much
lot
many
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "much"

Explanation:
☛ "Much" is the correct answer because it is used with uncountable nouns like "work."
☛ "Whole" is incorrect as it implies completeness, whereas the sentence refers to remaining work.
☛ "Lot" is used as "a lot of," not alone.
☛ "Many" is used with countable nouns, but "work" is uncountable.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Much is used with uncountable nouns (e.g., water, work, money).
☛ Many is used with countable nouns (e.g., books, apples, cars).
☛ A lot of can be used with both types of nouns but cannot stand alone.
question_hi:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.
Hurry up ! There’s still ________ work left to do.
options_hi: whole
much
lot
many
solution_hi:
Solution: Correct Answer is "much"

Explanation:
☛ यहाँ "much" सही विकल्प है क्योंकि यह अगणनीय संज्ञा (uncountable noun) "work" के साथ प्रयोग किया जाता है।
☛ "Whole" गलत है क्योंकि यह पूर्णता का बोध कराता है, जबकि वाक्य में शेष कार्य का जिक्र है।
☛ "Lot" का प्रयोग "a lot of" के रूप में होता है, अकेले नहीं।
☛ "Many" का प्रयोग गणनीय संज्ञाओं (countable nouns) के साथ होता है, जबकि "work" अगणनीय है।

Grammar Rules:
☛ Much का प्रयोग अगणनीय संज्ञाओं (जैसे—water, work, money) के साथ होता है।
☛ Many का प्रयोग गणनीय संज्ञाओं (जैसे—books, apples, cars) के साथ होता है।
☛ A lot of दोनों प्रकार की संज्ञाओं के साथ प्रयुक्त होता है, लेकिन इसे अकेले नहीं लगाया जा सकता।

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.
He gazed around the room ______ lay hidden a treasure chest.
options: whereof
whereby
wherein
whereas
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "wherein"

Explanation:
☛ The sentence describes a room in which a treasure chest is hidden.
☛ "Wherein" is a relative adverb that refers to a place and means 'in which' or 'where'.
☛ It connects two clauses and provides additional information about the first clause (room).
☛ Other options like "whereof" (of which), "whereby" (by which), and "whereas" (while) are incorrect because they indicate different relations (possession, means, contrast) rather than location.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Relative Adverbs (wherein, whereby, whereof, etc.) are used to connect clauses in complex sentences.
☛ "Wherein" specifically provides information about a place or situation.
☛ While choosing such words, pay attention to the context and the relation being expressed in the sentence.
question_hi:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.
He gazed around the room ______ lay hidden a treasure chest.
options_hi: whereof
whereby
wherein
whereas
solution_hi:
Solution: Correct Answer is "wherein"

Explanation:
☛ यहाँ वाक्य में एक ऐसे स्थान (room) का वर्णन किया गया है जिसमें एक खजाना छिपा हुआ है।
☛ "wherein" एक relative adverb है जो स्थान (place) से संबंधित जानकारी देता है और इसका अर्थ है 'जिसमें' या 'जहाँ पर'।
☛ यह दो clauses को जोड़ता है और पहले clause (room) के बारे में अतिरिक्त जानकारी प्रदान करता है।
☛ अन्य विकल्प जैसे "whereof" (जिसका), "whereby" (जिसके द्वारा), और "whereas" (जबकि) इस संदर्भ में उपयुक्त नहीं हैं क्योंकि वे स्थान के बजाय अन्य संबंधों को दर्शाते हैं।

Grammar Rules:
☛ Relative Adverbs (wherein, whereby, whereof, etc.) का प्रयोग complex sentences में clauses को जोड़ने के लिए किया जाता है।
☛ "Wherein" विशेष रूप से स्थान (place) या स्थिति (situation) से संबंधित जानकारी देता है।
☛ इन शब्दों का चयन करते समय वाक्य के context और संबंध (relation) पर ध्यान देना चाहिए।

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

We have requested Mrs. Nagpal _______ our play for this year’s annual function.
options: to direct
directed
directing
direct
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "to direct"

Explanation:
☛ The sentence uses 'requested' followed by 'to + verb (direct)' because 'request' is followed by 'to + infinitive'.
☛ 'Requested' is a transitive verb that requires an infinitive (to + verb) after it.
☛ 'Directed' (past tense) and 'directing' (present participle) are grammatically incorrect here as they do not fit with 'requested'.
☛ 'Direct' (base form) is also incorrect because 'request' is not followed by a bare infinitive.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Verbs like 'request', 'ask', and 'tell' are followed by 'to + infinitive'.
☛ The infinitive (to + verb) is used to express purpose, intention, or to indicate an action to be performed.
☛ Past participle (V3) and present participle (V1+ing) are used in passive voice and continuous tenses, which are not appropriate in this context.
question_hi:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

We have requested Mrs. Nagpal _______ our play for this year’s annual function.
options_hi: to direct
directed
directing
direct
solution_hi:
Solution: Correct Answer is "to direct"

Explanation:
☛ यहाँ वाक्य में 'requested' के बाद 'to + verb (direct)' का प्रयोग किया गया है क्योंकि 'request' के साथ 'to + infinitive' का प्रयोग होता है।
☛ 'Requested' एक transitive verb है जिसके बाद infinitive (to + verb) का प्रयोग किया जाता है।
☛ 'Directed' (past tense) और 'directing' (present participle) यहाँ व्याकरणिक रूप से गलत हैं क्योंकि वे 'requested' के साथ सही तालमेल नहीं बिठाते।
☛ 'Direct' (base form) भी गलत है क्योंकि 'request' के बाद bare infinitive का प्रयोग नहीं होता।

Grammar Rules:
☛ 'Request', 'ask', 'tell' जैसे verbs के बाद 'to + infinitive' का प्रयोग होता है।
☛ Infinitive (to + verb) का प्रयोग purpose, intention या किसी कार्य को करने के लिए कहने के लिए किया जाता है।
☛ Past participle (V3) और present participle (V1+ing) का प्रयोग passive voice और continuous tenses में होता है, जो यहाँ संदर्भ के अनुसार उपयुक्त नहीं है।

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

We saw some children ______ with one another as we were walking around.
options: quarrelling
quarrels
quarrelled
to quarrel
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "quarrelling"


Explanation:

☛The sentence uses Present Continuous Tense as the action (quarrel) describes an ongoing event at that moment.
☛After "We saw some children", the Verb+ing (Present Participle) form is used when an action is in progress simultaneously.
☛"quarrelling" here functions as an Object Complement, describing the state of "children".
☛Other options (quarrels, quarrelled, to quarrel) are grammatically incorrect in this context.



Grammar Rules:

☛Present Participle (Verb+ing) is used in Continuous Tenses and after Perception Verbs (see, hear, watch etc.).
☛After Perception Verbs, Object + Base Form (V1) suggests complete action, while Verb+ing suggests ongoing action.
☛Using Infinitive (to quarrel) would be incorrect here as it indicates future possibility, not ongoing action.
☛The simple past form "quarrelled" would change the meaning to a completed action rather than one in progress.
question_hi:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

We saw some children ______ with one another as we were walking around.
options_hi: quarrelling
quarrels
quarrelled
to quarrel
solution_hi:
Solution: Correct Answer is "quarrelling"


Explanation:

☛यहाँ वाक्य में Present Continuous Tense का प्रयोग हुआ है क्योंकि क्रिया (quarrel) एक निरंतर चल रही घटना को दर्शा रही है।
☛"We saw some children" के बाद Verb+ing (Present Participle) form का प्रयोग होता है जब कोई क्रिया उसी समय चल रही हो।
☛"quarrelling" यहाँ Object Complement के रूप में काम कर रहा है, जो "children" की स्थिति को describe कर रहा है।
☛अन्य विकल्प (quarrels, quarrelled, to quarrel) व्याकरणिक रूप से इस संदर्भ में गलत हैं।



Grammar Rules:

☛Present Participle (Verb+ing) का प्रयोग Continuous Tenses और After Perception Verbs (see, hear, watch etc.) में होता है।
☛Perception Verbs के बाद यदि Object + Base Form (V1) प्रयोग करें तो पूरी घटना का बोध होता है, जबकि Verb+ing प्रयोग करने पर क्रिया के जारी रहने का बोध होता है।
☛इस प्रकार के वाक्यों में Infinitive (to quarrel) का प्रयोग गलत होगा क्योंकि यह भविष्य की संभावना को दर्शाता है, न कि चल रही क्रिया को।

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I don’t think your sister is enjoying the party. She ______ at her watch for the last half an hour.
options: has been looking
had looked
has looked
had been looking
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "has been looking"


Explanation:

☛The sentence requires Present Perfect Continuous Tense because the action (looking) started in the past (for the last half an hour) and is still continuing.
☛"has been looking" is the correct structure of this tense - has/have + been + verb+ing.
☛Other options are incorrect:

☛"had looked" - Past Perfect Tense which isn't appropriate here
☛"has looked" - Present Perfect Tense which doesn't show continuity
☛"had been looking" - Past Perfect Continuous Tense which isn't relevant here


☛While selecting tense, always pay attention to time indicators (for the last half an hour).



Grammar Rules:

☛Present Perfect Continuous Tense is used for actions that started in the past and are still continuing in the present.
☛Its structure is: Subject + has/have + been + V1+ing + Object.
☛Time indicators like 'for/since + time period' are often used with this tense.
☛The word 'been' is mandatory in this tense and cannot be omitted.
question_hi:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I don’t think your sister is enjoying the party. She ______ at her watch for the last half an hour.
options_hi: has been looking
had looked
has looked
had been looking
solution_hi:
Solution: Correct Answer is "has been looking"


Explanation:

☛यहाँ वाक्य में Present Perfect Continuous Tense का प्रयोग होना चाहिए क्योंकि क्रिया (looking) पिछले आधे घंटे से जारी है और अभी भी चल रही है।
☛"has been looking" इस टेंस की सही संरचना है - has/have + been + verb+ing.
☛अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं:

☛"had looked" - Past Perfect Tense है जो यहाँ उचित नहीं
☛"has looked" - Present Perfect Tense है जो निरंतरता नहीं दिखाता
☛"had been looking" - Past Perfect Continuous Tense है जो यहाँ प्रासंगिक नहीं


☛काल (tense) का चयन करते समय हमेशा समय के संकेतक (for the last half an hour) पर ध्यान दें।



Grammar Rules:

☛Present Perfect Continuous Tense का प्रयोग उन क्रियाओं के लिए होता है जो अतीत में शुरू हुई हों और वर्तमान में भी जारी हों।
☛इसकी संरचना है: Subject + has/have + been + V1+ing + Object.
☛समय के संकेतक जैसे 'for/since + time period' इस टेंस के साथ अक्सर प्रयुक्त होते हैं।
☛इस टेंस में been का प्रयोग अनिवार्य है और इसे नहीं छोड़ा जा सकता।
